claims.text: A predictive model based on locally measured vibrational density of states can accurately identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity compositions in CoCrFeNi-based high-entropy-alloy thin-film libraries.
Multielement mixing produces local vibrational heterogeneities through variations in atomic mass and bonding.
Local vibrational heterogeneities suppress low-frequency vibrational modes that are important for heat transport.
Suppression of low-frequency vibrational modes enhances phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering caused by local disorder lowers phonon thermal conductivity.
Combinatorial sputtering can produce CoCrFeNi-based thin-film libraries with broad compositional gradients under uniform processing conditions.
Ultrafast optical pump-probe measurements using TDTR can capture the local vibrational properties needed as model inputs.
The model can quantitatively correlate local vibrational features with thermal conductivity.
Resolving local vibrational characteristics will reduce prediction error by more than 30% relative to conventional methods.
The approach will identify alloy compositions having thermal conductivity below approximately 1 W/mK.
Current prediction models typically rely on harmonic approximations or macroscopic compositional averages.
Current prediction models have higher prediction errors and identify low-thermal-conductivity regions less accurately than the proposed approach.
The proposed approach is primarily applicable to combinatorial gradient thin films in CoCrFeNi-type systems.
The validity of the approach for other processing conditions or alloy systems has not been established.
Ambient- and cryogenic-temperature measurements can test the model across the accessible compositional space.
Systematic prediction deviations greater than 30% would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe a consistent association between suppressed low-frequency modes and reduced thermal conductivity would falsify the proposed mechanism.
